title: Family and home
intro: Let's go home for a bit. Genii promises not to ask about your grades. Mostly.

cards.prompt: Your parents offer to help you get your own place. One catch: it has to be a ten-minute walk from theirs.
cards.teenPrompt: Someday, your parents offer to help pay for your first apartment. One catch: it has to be a ten-minute walk from theirs.

options.t: Deal. Free help and home-cooked dinners nearby.
Counter with a 20-minute drive. Close enough for soup, not pop-ins.
Say no. I'll find my own place, even if later.
Depends on how often 'nearby' means 'dropping by'.
Couldn't do it without their help anyway.

options: If they'd drop by without asking
If the area works for my school or job
If the help came with more strings later

cards.mask: looks like a housing perk; measures whether family help with family hopes feels like closeness or like a leash (R1, T19)

friend.prompt: {name}'s parents will help with a place, if it's a ten-minute walk from theirs. {name}…

a.t: Takes it. Close to family is a bonus.

b.t: Counters with a 20-minute drive. Soup yes, pop-ins no.

cards.prompt: You and your person: six years, a shared dog, a joint Costco card. Your aunt asks, 'So when's the wedding?'

options.t: Soon. Vows out loud, and Grandma crying in row one.
Never needed one. The dog is our marriage certificate.

cards.mask: looks like a nosy-aunt moment; measures whether commitment needs the classic ritual to count (R3, T21, T11B slight)

cards.prompt: Family rule: nobody eats until everyone's at the table. Your cousin is 40 minutes late. The dumplings are going cold.

options.t: Wait. Rule's a rule, even for cold dumplings.
Eat. Save them a plate and send a photo.

cards.mask: looks like a dinner standoff; measures whether a house rule holds when the situation makes it costly (L3, T25)

friend.prompt: {name}'s family rule: nobody eats till everyone's there. A cousin is 40 minutes late. {name}…

a.t: Waits. Rule's a rule, even for cold dumplings.

b.t: Eats. Saves a plate, sends the cousin a photo.

cards.prompt: Your cousin quit a big career to stay home with the baby. Their partner works now. Grandma is still recovering from the news. Your own home, someday?
cards.teenPrompt: Your friend's parent quit a big job to run the house and now wins every bake sale. The other parent runs the business. Your own home, someday?

options.t: Same energy. Mine could run that way too.
Love it for them. Mine would run classic.

cards.mask: looks like an opinion on another family; measures whether the new script is fine for others but not for you (R3, T20A split)

friend.prompt: {name}'s cousin quits a big career to stay home with the baby. Would {name} run a home that way?

b.t: Love it for them, classic for {name}.

cards.prompt: A parent needs someone with them every day for six months. They've told everyone they're 'totally fine.' Your siblings could help. Moving back would cost you at work.
cards.teenPrompt: A grandparent moves in and needs daily help for a few months. They insist they're 'totally fine.' Your family asks who can pitch in after school.

options.t: Say 'I've got it' before anyone else can answer.
Start a shift calendar. Watch who 'forgets' to accept.
Pitch a hired caregiver at dinner. Brace for the silence.
Wait to see who steps up, then fill the gaps.
Nobody else can. It lands on me either way.

cards.mask: looks like a logistics problem; measures whether you carry family need yourself or build a shared system around it (T18)

friend.prompt: Someone in {name}'s family needs daily care for months and insists they're 'totally fine.' What does {name} do first?

a.t: Says 'I've got it' before anyone else answers.

b.t: Starts a shift calendar so everyone takes turns.

cards.prompt: Big family wedding. 300 guests, an open bar, a toast that's on page six. You're the one…

options.t: Leading the family dance. I've known the steps since I was five.
Doing open-bar math. That's a whole used car.
Cornering the grandparents: 'Okay, 50 years. What's the trick?'
Timing the toast. We're on page four of six.
Herding three generations into one photo. Twice.
Running the kids' table. Great at it. Zero plans for my own.

cards.mask: looks like a wedding-guest cast list; measures whether a wedding is a family ritual worth the fuss or money better spent elsewhere (T21, 18+ only), with a no-kids line (T11B slight, the evidence judge's third T11B source). Fix pass round 2 made it behaviour in someone else's wedding so it no longer restates C6-7's own-celebration lines, and placed it four cards from C6-9 and C6-7

cards.prompt: Your family's last big 'absolutely not' to a plan of yours: a trip, a school, a move, a haircut. What did you actually do?

options.t: Did it anyway. Told them after it went fine.
Sent a sibling or an aunt in first to soften them up.
Dropped it. Peace at home was worth more.
Said I'd 'think about it.' Waited till they forgot, then did it.
Went with theirs. They were paying for it.

cards.mask: looks like a family argument story; measures whether your big calls are made together or by you (R1, T19)

friend.prompt: {name}'s family says 'absolutely not' to a plan. What does {name} do?

a.t: Sends a sibling or an aunt in first to soften them up.

b.t: Says 'I'll think about it,' waits till they forget, does it.

cards.prompt: Week one in a new place with your person or a roommate. The sink is full, the trash smells, and you're both just staring at it.
cards.teenPrompt: Your parents are away for the weekend. You and your sibling are in charge. By Saturday the sink is full and the trash smells.

options.t: Run it like home: nobody sits till the dishes are done.
Split by what we each hate least. I'll take trash.
Make a chore wheel. Spin it every Sunday. No appeals.
Bribe them with snacks to do all of it.
Do my half the way I was raised. Their half, their call.

cards.mask: looks like a chore standoff; measures whether a home runs on the inherited script or one you write from scratch (R3, T20). Plain classic scores R3 only; T20A comes only from the mixed line (my half classic, theirs their call)

friend.prompt: {name} moves in with someone. The sink is full and nobody moves. What does {name} do?

a.t: Runs it like home: nobody sits till the dishes are done.

b.t: Splits chores by what each of them hates least.

cards.prompt: Your parents want you to keep helping an adult sibling who never quite gets it together. In that story, you're the…
cards.teenPrompt: Your sibling keeps needing a rescue: homework, chores, cash. Your parents say, 'Help them, they're family.' In that story, you're the…

options.t: Bank. Open 24/7. No questions, no lecture.
Deadline. 'Last time' comes with an actual date.
Grumbler. I help, then vent about it all week.
Secret sponsor. I help, and nobody else knows.
Landlord. I help. Rent is my dishes for a week.
Referee. I tell my parents to stop asking me. They don't.

cards.mask: looks like a family cast list; measures whether your help to family is open-ended or has an end date (T18)

friend.prompt: {name}'s sibling keeps needing a rescue, and the parents say 'help, you're family.' {name} is the…

b.t: Deadline. 'Last time' comes with an actual date.

cards.prompt: Someday, your big celebration: a wedding, or whatever your version is. Your budget, your call. Pick the two that must happen.

options.t: Every relative there, even the ones I can't name.
Every ritual, in order, even the ones nobody can explain.
Something handed down: a ring, a dish, a song.
Ten people max. The best dinner of our lives.
Most of the money goes to a trip or a home.
Something nobody's done: a hike, a game night, a beach.

cards.mask: looks like party planning; measures whether a big life moment should follow the ritual or your own design (R3, T20B; plain classic picks score R3 only, never T20A; T21 scores for 18+ players only, per the library rule that locked18 tags fire only from 18+ play)

cards.prompt: The big family holiday. Someone suggests skipping the usual dinner this year and doing something totally different.

options.t: Absolutely not. Same dishes, same seats, same fight.
Yes! Karaoke room, takeout, everyone in pajamas.
Keep the one dish that matters. Reinvent the rest.
Do both: classic dinner first, the new thing after.

cards.mask: looks like holiday planning; measures whether tradition is the point or a starting draft (R3, T20). Plain classic scores R3 only; T20A sits on 'Do both', the mixed move (their new thing, my classic dinner); teen-safe R3 check, served in the finale (slot 3), not in chapter 6
